reduce:0.en: Inside the old lighthouse, the flame burned too bright. Old Helm turned a brass dial on the wall, and the roaring light began to *reduce* to a soft, steady glow. 'There,' he said, satisfied. The room felt calmer now, and the star map on the table became easier to read.
reduce:0.cnHint: 老舵转动黄铜旋钮，将灯塔的强光____到柔和的亮度，星图终于看清楚了。
reduce:0.hook: But the map now showed an island that wasn't there before.
reduce:0.line: 'We need to *reduce* the flame before the whole map burns away.'

process:0.en: Bell spread the torn map pieces across the lighthouse floor. 'Don't rush,' she said quietly. Each piece had to be placed in the right order. The *process* of fitting them together took nearly an hour, but slowly, a path between two floating islands appeared like a ribbon of light.
process:0.cnHint: 小铃耐心地将碎片一片片拼合，这个____需要将近一个小时才能完成。
process:0.hook: The final piece, though, was missing from the pile.
process:0.line: 'The *process* is slow, but every piece matters — trust me.'

able:0.en: The lighthouse staircase was steep and slick with sea mist. I climbed carefully, gripping the iron rail. At the top, I was finally *able* to see the full spread of floating islands outside the round window — dozens of them, glowing like embers in the dark sky above us.
able:0.cnHint: 我爬上灯塔顶层，终于____看清楚窗外所有悬浮岛屿的全貌。
able:0.hook: One island, far to the east, blinked like a dying star.
able:0.line: 'Once we fix the lens, we will be *able* to signal the others.'

drive:0.en: A fierce wind howled through a crack in the lighthouse wall. Old Helm said the same wind had once been used to *drive* a small mill wheel that powered the beacon lamp. Now the wheel was broken, and the whole room hummed with cold air looking for somewhere to go.
drive:0.cnHint: 老舵说这股风曾经用来____一个小磨轮为灯塔供电，但现在磨轮已经损坏了。
drive:0.hook: Without power, the beacon would go dark by midnight.
drive:0.line: 'This wind is strong enough to *drive* the wheel again — we just need rope.'

face:0.en: Hanging above the lighthouse door was a carved wooden *face* — round eyes, a wide open mouth, and smooth cheeks worn pale by salt air. Bell said the old sailors believed it watched the sea for danger. Tonight, its hollow eyes seemed pointed straight at the locked chest in the corner.
face:0.cnHint: 灯塔门上方挂着一张木雕____，小铃说水手们相信它会守望大海。
face:0.hook: The chest it seemed to watch had no visible lock at all.
face:0.line: 'Look at the *face* above the door — it is pointing at something.'

possible:0.en: Old Helm studied the star map with a small candle held close. 'It is *possible*,' he murmured, tracing a curved line with his finger, 'that the lighthouse was built here on purpose — right at the crossing point of three island routes.' Bell and I looked at each other with wide eyes.
possible:0.cnHint: 老舵认为灯塔建在这里____是有意为之，正好位于三条航线的交汇点。
possible:0.hook: If he was right, someone very clever had planned all of this long ago.
possible:0.line: 'Is it *possible* that this lighthouse is older than any island on the map?'

similar:0.en: Bell pulled two brass keys from her coat pocket and set them side by side on the lighthouse table. They looked nearly *similar* in shape, but one had a small notch on its edge that the other lacked. 'One opens something here,' she said, 'and one I found on the last island.'
similar:0.cnHint: 小铃拿出两把黄铜钥匙，它们外形____，但其中一把边缘有一个小缺口。
similar:0.hook: Neither key matched the lock on the chest in front of them.
similar:0.line: 'These two keys are *similar*, but only one of them belongs here.'

involve:0.en: Old Helm sat down and folded his hands. 'This mission will *involve* more than just collecting words,' he said slowly, looking at the glowing map spread across the lighthouse wall. 'It involves trust, timing, and a few leaps of faith across open sky.' Bell nodded. I swallowed quietly and nodded too.
involve:0.cnHint: 老舵告诉我们，这次任务将____更多挑战，不仅仅是收集词语那么简单。
involve:0.hook: He did not say what waited for us beyond the last island.
involve:0.line: 'Every great journey will *involve* moments when you cannot see the next step.'

develop:0.en: Inside the lighthouse, Old Helm spread a blank chart across the table. 'Every island we visit helps us *develop* a clearer picture of the sky,' he said, tracing a line with one careful finger. I watched the map slowly take shape and felt, for the first time, that I truly belonged to this troupe.
develop:0.cnHint: 老赫姆在灯塔内铺开地图，解释每次旅行都能帮助他们____出更清晰的航路图。
develop:0.hook: But one corner of the chart showed an island none of us had ever named.
develop:0.line: 'Every island we visit helps us *develop* a clearer picture of the sky.'

level:0.en: Bell climbed the spiral stairs and checked the old brass instrument fixed to the wall. 'The water inside this tube tells us our *level*,' she explained, tapping the glass gently. The bubble sat perfectly in the middle. The lighthouse floor was true, and so, it seemed, was our heading.
level:0.cnHint: 贝尔检查黄铜仪器，向我解释水管中的气泡如何指示灯塔地面的____。
level:0.hook: Then the bubble shifted, just slightly, toward the eastern wall.
level:0.line: 'The water inside this tube tells us our *level* — trust it.'

enjoy:0.en: Rain tapped softly against the lighthouse windows while we sat around the iron stove. Old Helm handed out warm drinks, and for a quiet hour we did nothing but *enjoy* the sound of the storm outside. Bell smiled at her cup. Even Silverfang set down his charts and simply listened.
enjoy:0.cnHint: 雨夜里，大家围坐在炉边，静静____着窗外风暴带来的宁静时光。
enjoy:0.hook: Then a shape moved past the glass — something large, and curious.
enjoy:0.line: 'Even on a stormy night, *enjoy* the stillness while it lasts.'

fact:0.en: I had always thought the lighthouse was abandoned, but Bell set me straight. 'The *fact* is, someone lit this lamp just three nights ago,' she said, pointing to the fresh oil in the base. The wick was still warm. Whoever had been here had left in a hurry.
fact:0.cnHint: 贝尔指着灯台底部的新鲜灯油，告诉我一个令人意外的____。
fact:0.hook: A single muddy boot print near the door pointed toward the upper stairs.
fact:0.line: 'The *fact* is, someone lit this lamp just three nights ago.'

news:0.en: Silverfang burst through the lighthouse door, shaking rain from his coat. 'I have *news*,' he announced, spreading a damp note on the table. It read: a second troupe had already claimed the eastern chain of islands. Old Helm studied the note in silence, then slowly began to smile.
news:0.cnHint: 竞争船长冲进灯塔，带来了一条关于另一支队伍的重要____。
news:0.hook: Old Helm's smile told me this was exactly the challenge he had been hoping for.
news:0.line: 'I have *news* — and it changes everything about our route.'

company:0.en: The lighthouse felt lonely when I first stepped inside, all cold stone and echoing steps. But Bell lit the lantern, Old Helm laid out supper, and soon the warm *company* of the troupe filled every corner. I realised a place is never really empty if the right people are in it with you.
company:0.cnHint: 灯塔起初显得冷清，但伙伴们的____让每个角落都充满了温暖。
company:0.hook: Outside, a second light blinked on the horizon — someone else had found this island too.
company:0.line: 'Good *company* turns even a cold lighthouse into a home.'

cost:0.en: Old Helm opened the supply chest and counted what remained. 'Crossing to the next island will *cost* us the last of our lamp oil,' he said quietly. We all looked at the single candle burning on the table. It was a real choice: stay safe in the light, or spend it and sail on.
cost:0.cnHint: 老赫姆清点物资，说明前往下一座岛屿将____掉他们最后的灯油。
cost:0.hook: Bell was already tying the sail — she had made her choice before he finished speaking.
cost:0.line: 'Crossing tonight will *cost* us the last of our oil — choose wisely.'

idea:0.en: Nobody could read the strange symbols carved into the lighthouse wall until I had a quiet *idea*: hold a candle behind the stone and look for shadows. The hidden lines lit up at once, forming a clear path between three islands we had never marked on our chart. Old Helm laughed with delight.
idea:0.cnHint: 我想到一个____，用烛光照射石壁，意外揭开了墙上神秘符号的秘密。
idea:0.hook: The path led straight toward the one island Bell had always refused to name.
idea:0.line: 'That *idea* of yours just opened a door we did not know existed.'

conversation:0.en: Inside the lighthouse, maps covered every wall. Old Helm sat beside a flickering lantern, deep in *conversation* with a keeper whose white hair reached the floor. I leaned close, catching words like 'northern star' and 'hidden gate.' Whatever they were sharing, it felt older than the islands themselves.
conversation:0.cnHint: 老舵手在灯塔内与守塔人进行了一场神秘的____，我悄悄旁听。
conversation:0.hook: The keeper's last whisper made Old Helm go pale.
conversation:0.line: 'This *conversation* must stay between us and these walls,' Old Helm said.

self:0.en: The lighthouse held a tall mirror, cracked down the middle. Bell stood before it, very still. 'You have to know your *self* before you can read the stars,' she said softly. I looked at my own reflection and felt, for the first time, like a true member of this troupe.
self:0.cnHint: 贝尔在灯塔的镜子前说，要了解____才能读懂星星。
self:0.hook: Then the mirror showed a reflection that was not Bell's.
self:0.line: 'Know your *self* first, or the stars will only confuse you,' Bell said.

age:0.en: The lighthouse keeper opened a worn logbook. 'This tower is from another *age*,' he said, tracing faded ink with one finger. The drawings inside showed islands that no longer appeared on any map. Old Helm turned each page slowly, as if afraid the paper might simply dissolve into dust.
age:0.cnHint: 守塔人向大家展示了一本来自另一个____的旧航海日志。
age:0.hook: One drawing showed our very ship — dated three hundred years ago.
age:0.line: 'A tower of this *age* has seen things we cannot imagine,' the keeper said.

future:0.en: Bell spread a blank chart across the lighthouse floor. 'Every word we collect shapes the *future* of our journey,' she said, pressing a glowing fragment onto the paper. Where she placed it, new coastlines appeared like ink spreading through water. The troupe leaned in, breath held, watching land form from nothing.
future:0.cnHint: 贝尔将发光的碎片放上地图，说这将塑造旅程的____。
future:0.hook: The final coastline formed the shape of an eye.
future:0.line: 'The *future* of our route depends on the words we find,' Bell said.

effect:0.en: Old Helm lit a small blue candle near the lighthouse lens. The *effect* was immediate — the beam split into colours, each one pointing toward a different island. The keeper clasped his hands and nodded. I grabbed my notebook, trying to sketch the pattern before the candle burned too low.
effect:0.cnHint: 老舵手点燃蜡烛，灯塔光束因此产生了奇妙的____。
effect:0.hook: One coloured beam pointed straight down, into the floor.
effect:0.line: 'Watch closely — the *effect* only lasts until the candle melts,' Old Helm said.

local:0.en: A *local* guide met us at the lighthouse door, wearing a coat stitched with tiny island shapes. She knew every creak of the tower and every gap in its stones. Old Helm exchanged words with her in a low voice, then turned to us with a rare smile. We had found an ally.
local:0.cnHint: 一位____向导在灯塔门口迎接了我们，对这座塔了如指掌。
local:0.hook: She said no outsider had ever climbed to the top and returned unchanged.
local:0.line: 'I am the *local* guide — nothing in this tower surprises me,' she said.

tend:0.en: Inside the lighthouse, rows of small plants grew in clay pots along the windowsill. 'I *tend* to them every morning,' the keeper explained. 'Each one marks a ship I guided safely home.' There were hundreds of pots. Bell touched one leaf gently, and I felt a quiet gratitude fill the room.
tend:0.cnHint: 守塔人说他每天早晨都会____照看窗台上的植物，每株代表一艘船。
tend:0.hook: One pot sat empty, its soil freshly turned, waiting.
tend:0.line: 'I *tend* to every plant the way I tend to every lost ship,' the keeper said.

term:0.en: The keeper used a strange *term* — 'star-lock' — to describe the lighthouse mechanism. Nobody in our troupe had heard it before. Bell wrote it down at once. Old Helm said that in the old sailing world, each tower had its own private language, passed from keeper to keeper like a secret key.
term:0.cnHint: 守塔人用了一个专业____描述灯塔机关，我们谁也没听说过。
term:0.hook: Bell's pen stopped moving when she read the term backwards.
term:0.line: 'That *term* belongs to this tower alone — guard it well,' the keeper said.

risk:0.en: Inside the old lighthouse, the staircase groaned under every step. 'One loose board could send us down,' Bell warned, holding her lamp high. Old Helm moved forward anyway. He chose to *risk* the climb because the word-map fragment glowed faintly at the very top, too precious to leave behind.
risk:0.cnHint: 老舵手决定____攀登摇摇欲坠的灯塔楼梯，因为顶部有珍贵的碎片在发光。
risk:0.hook: The next step cracked — and the lamp went out.
risk:0.line: 'I will *risk* the climb; that fragment is worth it,' said Old Helm.

success:0.en: We gathered around the lighthouse keeper's old table, spreading the word-map pieces under the warm glow of a lantern. After three careful tries, the fragments locked together with a soft click. Bell clapped her hands. Our *success* filled the dusty room with laughter, and a new island name shimmered into view.
success:0.cnHint: 碎片拼合成功，灯塔小屋里充满了欢笑，新岛屿的名字随之浮现。
success:0.hook: But the name on the map was one none of us recognised.
success:0.line: 'This *success* means a new island is waiting for us,' Bell said.

group:0.en: A *group* of small glowing birds had nested inside the lighthouse lamp room, each one carrying a tiny letter-shaped feather. Bell said they were called letter-larks, drawn to words like moths to fire. Old Helm asked us to sit quietly so the birds would not scatter before we could read their feathers.
group:0.cnHint: 一____发光小鸟巢居在灯室里，每只都携带着字母形状的羽毛。
group:0.hook: One lark tilted its head and spoke a single clear word.
group:0.line: 'This *group* of birds may hold the clue we need,' Old Helm whispered.

course:0.en: Old Helm unrolled a long chart across the lighthouse floor. The glowing lines on it showed not just islands but the *course* the troupe had followed over many years — every stop, every word collected, every sky crossed. Seeing it all at once made the journey feel both enormous and quietly beautiful.
course:0.cnHint: 老舵手展开航图，整个船团多年来走过的____一览无余。
course:0.hook: And one stretch of the route had never been travelled at all.
course:0.line: 'Of *course* this is the path — every word we found confirms it,' said Old Helm.

relationship:0.en: Bell dusted off two old portraits hanging inside the lighthouse. One showed a navigator, the other a lighthouse keeper. A faded note below explained their *relationship*: they had traded words for safe passage for thirty years. Without that quiet partnership, half the islands on our map would never have been found.
relationship:0.cnHint: 贝尔发现两幅旧画像，画中人的____揭示了地图上许多岛屿被发现的秘密。
relationship:0.hook: The note ended with a warning neither of them had ever shared aloud.
relationship:0.line: 'Their *relationship* built the very map we carry today,' Bell said softly.

form:0.en: At the top of the lighthouse, the star-light passing through the old lens began to *form* a shape on the wall — slow and steady, like ink spreading on wet paper. It was an outline of an island none of us had seen before, its edges sharp and clear, asking to be explored.
form:0.cnHint: 星光穿过旧镜头，在墙上慢慢____出一座从未见过的岛屿轮廓。
form:0.hook: The outline pulsed once, then began to fade fast.
form:0.line: 'Watch it *form* — that island is real, I am certain,' Bell breathed.

interest:0.en: Old Helm picked up a dusty logbook from the lighthouse shelf and flipped through pages of careful notes. One entry caught his eye: a keeper had written about an island that vanished at dawn. His *interest* sharpened immediately. He read the passage aloud twice, his voice quiet, as if the words themselves might hear him.
interest:0.cnHint: 老舵手在航海日志中发现一条关于消失岛屿的记录，____一下子被勾了起来。
interest:0.hook: The date on that entry matched today's date exactly.
interest:0.line: 'My *interest* in this logbook just doubled — listen to this entry,' Old Helm said.

simply:0.en: Bell tried every key on the lighthouse keeper's old ring, one after another, until the last one turned. The hidden drawer opened to reveal a single folded word-map. She laughed, surprised. 'All that searching,' she said, 'and the answer was *simply* here, sitting in the dark, waiting patiently for someone to look.'
simply:0.cnHint: 贝尔试遍所有钥匙，最终发现答案____就藏在抽屉里，静静等待。
simply:0.hook: The map inside showed a lighthouse — identical to the one they stood in.
simply:0.line: 'It was *simply* here the whole time — no mystery at all,' Bell laughed.

suggest:0.en: Inside the old lighthouse, dust covered every shelf. Bell held up a cracked lens and pointed to the faded marks around its edge. 'These scratches *suggest* someone was here recently,' she said. Old Helm nodded slowly, his lantern casting long shadows across the stone floor.
suggest:0.cnHint: 小铃检查破损的镜片，从划痕中____出有人最近到访过。
suggest:0.hook: But the door had been locked from the inside.
suggest:0.line: 'These marks *suggest* we are not the first ones here.'

improve:0.en: Old Helm spread the star charts across the lighthouse table. Several routes were marked in faded ink. 'If we *improve* this path here,' Bell said, tracing a new line with her finger, 'we can reach the next island before the storm clouds gather.' The troupe leaned in, hopeful.
improve:0.cnHint: 小铃研究星图，认为可以____现有的航线来赶在风暴前抵达。
improve:0.hook: Then the charts slid off the table on their own.
improve:0.line: 'We can *improve* this route and still reach the island in time.'

affect:0.en: A strange blue mist crept under the lighthouse door. Bell pressed her hand to the cold glass of the window. 'That mist could *affect* the compass readings,' she warned. Old Helm quickly covered the instruments with his coat. Outside, the floating islands drifted in and out of view.
affect:0.cnHint: 奇怪的蓝色雾气从门缝钻入，小铃担心它会____罗盘的读数。
affect:0.hook: The compass needle had already begun to spin.
affect:0.line: 'That mist will *affect* our instruments if we are not careful.'

support:0.en: A wide crack ran up the inner wall of the lighthouse. Old Helm pressed his palm against the cold stone. 'This pillar once gave *support* to the whole upper floor,' he said quietly. Bell looked up at the ceiling, which groaned as the wind passed. We all stood very still.
support:0.cnHint: 老舵发现墙上的裂缝，解释那根柱子曾是整层楼的____。
support:0.hook: A second groan answered the first, louder than before.
support:0.line: 'Without *support*, the whole upper floor could come down tonight.'

hand:0.en: The old lighthouse keeper had left one thing behind: a small notebook. I opened it and found, on the last page, a careful drawing of a door hidden in the rock. Bell reached over and offered her *hand* to steady the book as the night wind pushed through the cracks.
hand:0.cnHint: 在灯塔旧笔记本的最后一页，小铃伸出____帮我稳住书页。
hand:0.hook: The hidden door in the drawing matched the wall behind us.
hand:0.line: 'Here, let me give you a *hand* with that old book.'

finding:0.en: Old Helm read aloud from the lighthouse log. Entry after entry described strange lights on the eastern island. His voice slowed at the last line. 'This *finding* changes everything,' he said, setting the log down. Bell and I looked at each other. The lights he described matched what we had seen.
finding:0.cnHint: 老舵朗读灯塔日志，最后一条____让大家面面相觑。
finding:0.hook: The date on that last entry was last night.
finding:0.line: 'This *finding* in the log changes every plan we made.'

ago:0.en: Dust lay thick on the lighthouse windowsill. Bell blew it away gently and uncovered a small carving: a ship inside a circle. 'Someone made this a long time *ago*,' she said softly. Old Helm crouched beside her and studied it with his lantern. The carving matched the symbol on our map.
ago:0.cnHint: 小铃在窗台灰尘下发现一幅雕刻，那是很久____有人留下的印记。
ago:0.hook: Our map had been made by whoever stood in this room.
ago:0.line: 'Someone carved this long *ago*, and left it here for us.'

essay:0.en: On the lighthouse desk lay a single sheet of paper, covered in neat, small writing. Old Helm read it carefully. 'It reads like an *essay*,' he said, 'a careful argument that the islands move in a pattern.' Bell's eyes lit up. If that pattern was real, we could predict where the next island would appear.
essay:0.cnHint: 桌上的纸张像一篇____，详细论述了浮岛移动的规律。
essay:0.hook: The final sentence named the island we were searching for.
essay:0.line: 'This *essay* explains exactly why the islands keep moving.'

popular:0.en: Inside the lighthouse, shelves lined every wall. Old Helm pulled out a worn song book and smiled. 'This tune is *popular* among island folk,' he said softly, humming a few bright notes. The melody filled the round room like warm light, and even Bell tapped her foot without thinking.
popular:0.cnHint: 老舵手在灯塔内发现一本歌谱，说这首曲子在岛上非常____。
popular:0.hook: But the last page held no song — only a map.
popular:0.line: 'This tune is *popular* among every sailor who passes through.'

current:0.en: Bell spread her chart across the lighthouse floor and traced a thin blue line with her finger. 'The *current* wind pattern pushes clouds away from the north tower,' she said, frowning. That single fact changed everything about our route. Old Helm nodded slowly and began folding the old map away.
current:0.cnHint: 领航员查看图表，发现____的风向对路线有重要影响。
current:0.hook: Something above us groaned — the tower was already turning.
current:0.line: 'The *current* wind will not wait; we must decide now.'

difficult:0.en: The lighthouse logbook was old and the ink had faded badly. I tried to read aloud, but every other line made no sense. Old Helm leaned over my shoulder. 'Navigation language is *difficult* at first,' he said gently, 'but the patterns will come to you.' I turned the page and tried again.
difficult:0.cnHint: 我尝试阅读航海日志，发现里面的语言很____，老舵手鼓励我继续。
difficult:0.hook: Then one faded word on page nine made my hands shake.
difficult:0.line: 'Navigation language is *difficult*, but you will learn its rhythm.'

amount:0.en: Silverfang stepped inside, shaking rain from her coat. She dropped a small pouch on the table with a heavy clink. 'That *amount* of star-coins should cover the toll for the upper beacon,' she said coolly. Old Helm counted the coins without a word, then looked up with an expression I could not read.
amount:0.cnHint: 竞争船长带来了一定____的星币，说够支付上层灯塔的通行费。
amount:0.hook: Old Helm pushed two coins back across the table.
amount:0.line: 'That *amount* of star-coins is exactly what the beacon keeper demands.'

point:0.en: Old Helm tapped the centre of the lighthouse map with one firm finger. 'This *point* is where all three beacon lights cross at midnight,' he said. Bell looked up sharply. I leaned closer and saw a tiny symbol there — a shape none of us had noticed before in all our travels together.
point:0.cnHint: 老舵手指出地图上的一个关键____，三道灯光在午夜交汇于此。
point:0.hook: The symbol began to glow the moment the clock struck twelve.
point:0.line: 'This *point* on the map is where the real door opens.'

role:0.en: 'Each of us has a *role* tonight,' Old Helm said, standing at the centre of the lighthouse. Bell would read the stars, Silverfang would handle the signal mirror, and I would keep the log. It felt small, but Old Helm caught my doubtful look and smiled. 'Every role matters,' he added quietly.
role:0.cnHint: 老舵手宣布今晚每个人都有自己的____，我负责记录。
role:0.hook: Then the lighthouse beam went dark, and no one had touched it.
role:0.line: 'Every *role* in this tower matters — especially yours tonight.'

enable:0.en: Inside the lighthouse, Bell pointed to a brass panel covered in small levers. 'Each lever controls a different lamp,' she said. I reached up and pulled the last one. A deep hum filled the room, and the great beam began to spin. Old Helm nodded. 'That should *enable* us to read the sky map tonight.'
enable:0.cnHint: 贝尔指导我操作黄铜面板，成功让灯塔运转，____了今晚阅读天空地图的可能。
enable:0.hook: But the map showed an island none of us had ever heard of.
enable:0.line: 'That should *enable* us to read the sky map tonight,' Old Helm said.

simple:0.en: The lighthouse keeper's table held only three things: a candle, a worn notebook, and a cup of cold tea. Old Helm picked up the notebook and smiled. 'The answer was always this *simple*,' he said softly. Inside, drawn in careful pencil lines, was a complete chart of the next five islands.
simple:0.cnHint: 老舵手在灯塔守夜人的桌上发现了一本笔记本，答案原来如此____。
simple:0.hook: One island on the chart had no name, only a question mark.
simple:0.line: 'The answer was always this *simple*,' Old Helm said softly.

several:0.en: We had been inside the lighthouse for *several* hours, sorting through boxes of old maps stacked against the curved walls. Bell held each one up to the lamp, looking for the hidden ink that only light could reveal. My arms ached, but I kept searching. Then she gasped.
several:0.cnHint: 我们在灯塔里花了____个小时翻找旧地图，贝尔突然倒吸一口凉气。
several:0.hook: The hidden ink spelled out a single word: danger.
several:0.line: 'We have been in here for *several* hours,' Bell said, stretching her arms.

struggle:0.en: The old winch that turned the lighthouse lens was rusted stiff. I gripped the iron handle with both hands and pulled. Bell counted aloud to keep my rhythm. It was a real *struggle*, but at last the gears gave a loud crack and the lens began to move, casting its first pale beam across the dark.
struggle:0.cnHint: 我努力转动生锈的绞盘，这场____终于有了结果，灯塔的镜片开始转动了。
struggle:0.hook: The beam swept across the clouds and lit up something huge.
struggle:0.line: 'I know it is a *struggle*, but keep turning!' Bell called out.

decision:0.en: Old Helm spread two maps across the lighthouse floor. One showed a safe, slow path south. The other pointed north, into the cloud belt, where stronger winds and stranger islands waited. He looked at Bell, then at me. 'This *decision* belongs to all three of us,' he said quietly.
decision:0.cnHint: 老舵手把两张地图摊在地板上，这个____需要我们三人共同做出。
decision:0.hook: I looked north and felt something pull at my chest like a tide.
decision:0.line: 'This *decision* belongs to all three of us,' Old Helm said.

kid:0.en: High on the lighthouse wall hung a small painting: a *kid* in an oversized coat, standing at a ship's wheel, eyes full of stars. Bell laughed softly. 'That was Old Helm, long ago.' I stared at the tiny figure and felt something warm settle in my chest. Every great captain starts somewhere.
kid:0.cnHint: 墙上的画里有一个穿着大号外套的____，贝尔说那是年轻时的老舵手。
kid:0.hook: Old Helm walked past the painting without a single glance.
kid:0.line: 'That *kid* in the painting believed every island could be reached,' Bell said.

ability:0.en: The lighthouse lens had cracked down the middle, and no one knew if it could still work. Silverfang crossed his arms. 'I doubt your *ability* to fix it without the right tools,' he said. I said nothing. I found a curved piece of spare glass in a crate and held it in place. The beam held steady.
ability:0.cnHint: 竞争船长怀疑我修复灯塔镜片的____，但我用一块备用玻璃证明了他是错的。
ability:0.hook: Silverfang stared at the steady beam and said nothing at all.
ability:0.line: 'I doubt your *ability* to fix it without the right tools,' Silverfang said.

task:0.en: Old Helm handed me a small brush and pointed to the great lens at the top of the lighthouse. 'Your *task* is to clean every inch before dawn,' he said. I climbed the iron stairs alone, brush in hand. By the time the first stars appeared, the glass blazed like a second moon.
task:0.cnHint: 老舵手交给我一个____：在黎明前把巨大的灯塔镜片擦干净。
task:0.hook: In the clean glass I saw a reflection of an island I did not recognise.
task:0.line: 'Your *task* is to clean every inch before dawn,' Old Helm said.

put:0.en: The lighthouse keeper's room was crowded with old charts. Old Helm picked up a glowing word-stone and *put* it carefully at the centre of the table. The moment it touched the wood, lines of light spread outward like rivers finding the sea, and a new island took shape in the air above us.
put:0.cnHint: 老舵手将发光的词石____在桌子中央，新的岛屿轮廓随即浮现在空中。
put:0.hook: The island in the light blinked once, then began to move.
put:0.line: '*Put* it right here — the stone needs to touch the centre.'

difference:0.en: Bell held two charts side by side under the lighthouse lamp. 'Look,' she said quietly. I leaned in and finally saw it — a single island drawn on one chart but missing from the other. That small *difference* was the only clue we had to find the path forward.
difference:0.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔灯光下对比两张地图，发现了关键的____，那是通往下一座岛屿的唯一线索。
difference:0.hook: Someone had removed that island from the newer chart on purpose.
difference:0.line: 'That *difference* between the two charts — that is exactly what we need.'

lack:0.en: The lighthouse had not been lit for years. I could feel the *lack* of warmth the moment we stepped inside — cold stone, dusty shelves, and a silence so heavy it pressed against my ears. Old Helm said nothing; he simply opened his pack and began to work.
lack:0.cnHint: 灯塔内部寒冷而寂静，旅团一进门就感受到了光与温暖的____。
lack:0.hook: Then something at the very top of the tower began to glow on its own.
lack:0.line: 'The *lack* of light here has kept the next island hidden for years.'

case:0.en: On the highest shelf sat a dusty wooden box. Bell lifted its lid and we all held our breath. Inside, resting on faded cloth, was a word-stone shaped like a tiny compass. 'In every *case* we have opened,' Old Helm murmured, 'the stone was waiting for the right hands.'
case:0.cnHint: 在灯塔最高处的架子上，小铃打开了一个木____，里面静静躺着一枚罗盘形状的词石。
case:0.hook: The compass needle swung hard toward the sealed door behind us.
case:0.line: 'In this *case*, I believe the stone chose to wait for you.'

sure:0.en: I reached for the word-stone, then paused. The light around it pulsed like a slow heartbeat. 'Are you *sure* it is safe?' I asked. Old Helm smiled the way he always did when he already knew the answer. 'Touch it,' he said. 'The island will not unlock itself.'
sure:0.cnHint: 旅团新成员伸手去拿词石时犹豫了，老舵手笑着说，____可以触碰，岛屿不会自己解锁。
sure:0.hook: My fingers brushed the stone — and the whole lighthouse shook.
sure:0.line: 'I am *sure* — the stone will not harm you, not tonight.'

enough:0.en: We had collected seven word-stones that month. Old Helm spread them on the lighthouse floor and counted twice. 'Seven is *enough*,' he said, pressing them together into a single shape. The pieces locked with a soft sound, and light poured through the cracks like sunrise through leaves.
enough:0.cnHint: 老舵手将七枚词石拼在一起，告诉大家这已经____，拼图完成的瞬间光芒从缝隙中涌出。
enough:0.hook: The joined stone rose slowly off the floor without anyone touching it.
enough:0.line: 'Seven stones — that is *enough* to open the next gate.'

attention:0.en: Bell was tracing the wall of the lighthouse with one careful finger. 'Pay *attention* to this part,' she said, and we gathered close. Beneath a layer of dust was a carving — the outline of an island none of our charts had ever shown, waiting quietly for someone to notice it.
attention:0.cnHint: 小铃提醒大家把____集中到灯塔墙壁上，灰尘下面藏着一座从未出现在地图上的岛屿轮廓。
attention:0.hook: The carving was still warm, as if someone had made it very recently.
attention:0.line: '*Attention*, everyone — look at what is hiding under this dust.'

certain:0.en: Old Helm studied the strange carving for a long time. Finally he straightened up. 'I am *certain* this is the Wandering Isle,' he said in a low voice. 'It moves. No chart can hold it.' Silverfang crossed her arms and looked at the ceiling, but even she did not argue.
certain:0.cnHint: 老舵手端详那幅雕刻后，____地认出那是传说中会移动的流浪岛，连竞争船长也沉默了。
certain:0.hook: Outside, the wind changed direction as though the island had heard its name.
certain:0.line: 'I am *certain* — that island has been waiting for this troupe.'

survey:0.en: Inside the old lighthouse, Bell spread a crinkled chart across the floor and began to *survey* every corner of the room. She checked the walls, the lantern housing, and even the dusty shelves. 'The word we need is hidden in here somewhere,' she said. After a long look, she pointed at a faint inscription above the door.
survey:0.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔内部仔细____每一个角落，终于发现了门框上方隐约的文字。
survey:0.hook: The inscription began to glow the moment her finger touched it.
survey:0.line: 'Let me *survey* the room before we touch anything,' Bell said.

care:0.en: The lighthouse keeper's old desk sat in the centre of the room, covered in papers. Old Helm picked up a fragile map with great *care*, holding it at the edges so his fingers would not smear the faded ink. 'Every word on this page is a door,' he murmured. The candle beside him flickered, and for a moment the whole room held its breath.
care:0.cnHint: 老赫尔姆以极大的____拿起那张脆弱的地图，生怕指尖的油脂晕开了墨迹。
care:0.hook: One smudge, and the door it described would vanish forever.
care:0.line: 'Handle it with *care* — one tear and the path is gone,' Old Helm said.

state:0.en: After climbing three flights of spiral stairs, I reached the lamp room. Everything was in a strange *state* — glass cracked, gears frozen, and the great lens tilted at an odd angle. Old Helm stepped in behind me and let out a slow breath. 'Someone left in a hurry,' he said. A thin layer of star-dust covered every surface, untouched for years.
state:0.cnHint: 灯塔顶层的一切都处于奇怪的____，仿佛有人曾仓皇离去。
state:0.hook: Then we noticed the footprints in the star-dust led only inward, never out.
state:0.line: 'Look at the *state* of this place — no one has been here for years,' Old Helm said.

impact:0.en: Bell dropped a brass coin onto the stone floor to test its echo, and the sharp *impact* sent a clear ring bouncing off every wall of the round room. The sound faded — and then, slowly, a hidden panel in the wall slid open. We looked at each other. 'Sound is the key,' Bell whispered, already reaching for her small drum.
impact:0.cnHint: 铜币落地的____声在圆形房间内回荡，竟震开了墙上一块隐藏的板壁。
impact:0.hook: Behind the panel, a second staircase curled down into perfect darkness.
impact:0.line: 'The *impact* of the coin on stone — that is what opens it,' Bell said.

reason:0.en: Silverfang studied the lighthouse log for a long time, frowning. 'There is a *reason* this beacon went dark ten years ago,' he said at last, tapping a page near the end. The final entry was a single sentence in a careful hand: the word for the next island had been found, and the keeper had left to follow it. The log snapped shut with a satisfying click.
reason:0.cnHint: 银牙翻阅灯塔日志，终于找到了灯塔熄灭的____——前任守灯人已独自出发去追寻下一座岛屿。
reason:0.hook: The keeper's name matched the carving on our oldest map fragment.
reason:0.line: 'There is a *reason* this light went out — and we just found it,' Silverfang said.

close:0.en: The word fragment was etched on the inside of the lens, tiny and easy to miss. I had to press my face *close* to the cold glass to read it. My breath fogged the surface and the letters blurred for a heart-stopping second. Then the fog cleared, and the word shone back at me like a small, steady star.
close:0.cnHint: 叙述者把脸凑得很____，才能看清刻在镜片内侧的词语碎片。
close:0.hook: The word was already vibrating faintly, as if eager to be spoken aloud.
close:0.line: 'Come *close* and read it carefully — one letter wrong and it fades,' Bell warned.

individual:0.en: Old Helm laid five word-fragments on the table and asked each of us to study one. 'Every *individual* piece matters,' he said. 'Miss even one and the map stays dark.' I stared at mine — a curve and two dots — and slowly understood that it was not a letter at all, but a tiny drawing of an island seen from above.
individual:0.cnHint: 老赫尔姆让每人负责一块碎片，强调每一个____的词语碎片都不可忽视。
individual:0.hook: My fragment trembled in my palm, pulling gently toward the north wall.
individual:0.line: 'Each *individual* fragment holds part of the route — lose one and we are lost,' Old Helm said.

area:0.en: Bell drew a circle on the chart with her fingertip. 'This *area* near the top of the lighthouse,' she said, 'does not match any island we have visited.' The circled space was blank — no name, no depth lines, just empty paper. Old Helm smiled for the first time all evening. Blank space on a troupe map meant only one thing: somewhere new to go.
area:0.cnHint: 小铃在海图上圈出灯塔顶部附近的一片____，那里空白一片，正是尚未到访的新岛屿。
area:0.hook: Old Helm reached for the blank space, and the paper glowed beneath his hand.
area:0.line: 'This *area* on the chart is empty — which means we have not been there yet,' Bell said.

suggest:1.en: The old lighthouse stood at the edge of the nearest floating island, its beam sweeping the dark. Bell studied the cracks in its stone wall and turned to Old Helm. 'These patterns *suggest* the tower was built long before our maps show,' she said, tracing a line with her finger.
suggest:1.cnHint: 小铃仔细查看灯塔裂缝，向老舵____这座塔比地图显示的更古老。
suggest:1.hook: But the cracks kept moving, slowly, like breathing.
suggest:1.line: 'These marks *suggest* someone was here long before us.'

improve:1.en: Old Helm climbed the spiral steps of the lighthouse, testing each one. Near the top, he pulled a bent iron rod from his pack and wedged it under a broken rung. 'This will *improve* our chances of reaching the lamp room,' he said, pressing his weight down until the step held firm.
improve:1.cnHint: 老舵用一根铁棒修固台阶，试图____攀登灯塔的条件。
improve:1.hook: From above came a low groan, as if the tower disagreed.
improve:1.line: 'A small fix can *improve* everything, trust me.'

affect:1.en: A cold wind rolled off the edge of the island and hit us as we stood before the lighthouse door. I watched it *affect* the flame inside the cracked lantern — it flickered, dimmed, then caught again, stubborn and bright. Old Helm nodded slowly, as if the flame had just answered a question.
affect:1.cnHint: 强风____了灯塔内的火焰，但火焰顽强地重新亮了起来。
affect:1.hook: Old Helm whispered, 'That flame should have gone out years ago.'

support:1.en: The outer walkway of the lighthouse had lost two of its pillars. Bell tested the railing and shook her head. 'We need *support* along this side before anyone walks out there,' she told us, already dragging a wooden beam from the supply cart. I grabbed the other end without being asked.
support:1.cnHint: 小铃发现走廊缺少____，要求大家一起搬来木梁加固。
support:1.hook: The railing snapped anyway, spinning silently into the clouds below.
support:1.line: 'Without *support* on this side, the whole walkway will fall.'

hand:1.en: The lighthouse door had not opened in years. Its lock was rusted into a solid block. Old Helm reached into his coat and produced a thin iron key, then offered me his other *hand* — steady, unhurried — as I balanced on the narrow stone ledge beside him while he worked the lock free.
hand:1.cnHint: 老舵打开锈锁时，向我伸出了____，帮我在狭窄石台上保持平衡。
hand:1.hook: The door swung open onto a room full of moving shadows.
hand:1.line: 'Take my *hand* — the ledge is narrower than it looks.'

finding:1.en: Inside the lamp room we discovered a journal wedged behind the great lens. Bell read it aloud while Old Helm held the lantern close. The most surprising *finding* was a hand-drawn map tucked between the last pages — a map of islands none of us had ever heard of, marked in red ink.
finding:1.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔灯室里读到了一本日志，最重要的____是夹在最后几页里的神秘地图。
finding:1.hook: Every island on that map carried the same single warning word.
finding:1.line: 'The strangest *finding* is this map — it shows islands off every chart.'

ago:1.en: Old Helm ran his thumb along an inscription carved into the lighthouse base. 'A troupe like ours lit this lamp a hundred years *ago*,' he read slowly, his voice going quiet. I looked up at the beam still turning above us and felt something close to pride, as if that old troupe were watching.
ago:1.cnHint: 老舵读到碑文，得知一百年____曾有人在此点亮灯塔。
ago:1.hook: The inscription had one more line, still too worn to read.
ago:1.line: 'A troupe lit this beacon a hundred years *ago*, just like us.'

essay:1.en: Tucked inside the journal was a folded sheet of paper — a short *essay* written in careful letters, describing the lighthouse as 'a door between known sky and unknown sky.' Bell read it twice, then folded it back and slipped it into her coat as if it were something rare and worth keeping safe.
essay:1.cnHint: 小铃在日志里发现了一篇____，将灯塔描述为已知天空与未知天空之间的门。
essay:1.hook: The last sentence of the essay named our troupe by name.
essay:1.line: 'This *essay* was written for someone who would come exactly here.'

develop:1.en: The old lighthouse stood at the edge of the island, its stone walls covered in strange carvings. Old Helm traced one with a careful finger. 'This place used to *develop* new star-charts,' he said softly. I looked up: each carving was a sky map, layer upon layer, growing outward like rings in water.
develop:1.cnHint: 老灯塔的墙上刻满了星图，老舵主说这里曾用来____新的航海图。
develop:1.hook: One carving on the highest stone still glowed faintly blue.
develop:1.line: 'We used to *develop* every star-chart right here on this very wall.'

level:1.en: Bell climbed the lighthouse stairs ahead of me, counting each step aloud. At the third *level* she stopped and pressed her ear to the wall. A low hum filled the air. 'The light still works,' she whispered, eyes wide. Outside the windows, clouds drifted far below us like a soft white sea.
level:1.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔的某一____停下来，发现灯塔的灯还在运转。
level:1.hook: Below those clouds, something enormous was slowly rising.
level:1.line: 'Stop at this *level* — the hum is strongest right here.'

enjoy:1.en: We found a stone bench facing the open sky, and Old Helm unwrapped a small bundle of rice cakes. 'We *enjoy* these moments,' he said, handing one to me with a warm smile. The stars were just appearing, pale and shy. For a little while, the next island could wait, and the whole sky felt like ours.
enjoy:1.cnHint: 在灯塔旁，大家停下来____这片星空下难得的宁静时光。
enjoy:1.hook: Then a new star blinked on — in exactly the wrong part of the sky.
enjoy:1.line: 'Sit down and *enjoy* the quiet — the stars are just waking up.'

fact:1.en: Silverfang spread a worn map on the lighthouse floor and jabbed it with one claw-tipped finger. 'The *fact* is, no one has reached the next island in twenty years,' he said flatly. Old Helm did not argue. I stared at the blank patch of map beyond the lighthouse mark, feeling the size of the unknown press against my chest.
fact:1.cnHint: 竞争船长直言说出一个____：二十年来没有人到达过下一座岛。
fact:1.hook: Old Helm's eyes said he knew exactly why — and was not telling.
fact:1.line: 'The *fact* is, this lighthouse has been dark for twenty years.'

news:1.en: A small wind-bird, made of folded paper and star-dust, fluttered down and landed on my arm. It carried a strip of thin cloth. Bell read it quickly, then looked up with bright eyes. 'Good *news*,' she said, 'the bridge-island is closer than we thought.' Old Helm tucked the cloth into his coat and pointed east, where the sky was already turning silver.
news:1.cnHint: 一只纸折的风鸟送来了____，说前方的桥岛比预想的近得多。
news:1.hook: The bird shook its wings once, then dissolved into ordinary dust.
news:1.line: 'This *news* changes everything — we leave at first light.'

company:1.en: The lighthouse top was cold and open to the wind, but nobody moved to go back down. Standing close together, watching the island chain stretch off into the dark, I understood what Old Helm had meant when he first asked me to join. The real gift was not the journey — it was the *company* along the way. Even Silverfang was quiet, and that felt like warmth.
company:1.cnHint: 在灯塔顶端，叙述者明白了旅途中最宝贵的是彼此的____。
company:1.hook: Far below, the troupe's small ship rocked, as if eager to move on.
company:1.line: 'Out here, good *company* is worth more than any map fragment.'

cost:1.en: Old Helm showed me a faded list carved beside the lighthouse door: names of words already collected, and beside each one a small mark. 'Every word has a *cost*,' he said quietly. 'You spend something to learn it — time, comfort, a little fear.' I ran my thumb over the marks. They felt less like warnings and more like proud little scars.
cost:1.cnHint: 老舵主在灯塔门边指着刻痕说，每个词的____都是一段亲身经历。
cost:1.hook: My own name was not on the list yet, but a blank space waited at the bottom.
cost:1.line: 'Every word we collect has a *cost*, and that is what makes it real.'

idea:1.en: I stared at the dark gap between our island and the next, trying to picture a path. Then Bell crouched down and drew a curve in the dust with one finger. 'What if we ride the light-current at dawn?' she said. It was a small *idea*, almost silly — but Old Helm's face opened into a slow grin. Sometimes the best plans start exactly that way.
idea:1.cnHint: 小铃蹲下来在尘土里画了一条线，提出了一个____，让大家眼前一亮。
idea:1.hook: Old Helm was already turning toward the ship before she even finished speaking.
idea:1.line: 'That *idea* of yours just might be the strangest thing that saves us.'

conversation:1.en: At the edge of Lantern Isle, Old Helm stopped beside a crumbling stone post. A local keeper sat there, eyes half-closed. Old Helm dropped a coin on the post, and a long *conversation* began — word by careful word — about a lighthouse that no map showed.
conversation:1.cnHint: 老舵在灯塔岛边缘与一位老人展开了一场关于神秘灯塔的____。
conversation:1.hook: The keeper's last word made Old Helm's hand go still.
conversation:1.line: 'That *conversation* gave us more than any map could,' Old Helm said.

self:1.en: Bell stood alone at the cliff's edge, staring at the lighthouse beam sweeping over the dark water. The troupe had split to search different paths, and for the first time she felt her *self* separate from the group — a single lantern apart from the fire.
self:1.cnHint: 贝尔独自站在悬崖边，第一次感受到独立的____。
self:1.hook: Then she saw a second beam, moving the wrong way.
self:1.line: 'You have to trust your *self* out here,' Bell said softly.

age:1.en: Old Helm ran his fingers along the lighthouse wall. The stone was deeply worn, and the carved marks near the door told of an earlier *age* — a time when the floating islands were still new and the sky roads had not yet been named.
age:1.cnHint: 老舵抚摸灯塔石墙，石刻记录着一个遥远____的秘密。
age:1.hook: One mark was still warm to the touch.
age:1.line: 'This lighthouse has stood since an *age* before any of us,' Old Helm murmured.

future:1.en: Silverfang climbed to the lighthouse platform and looked out across the chain of islands stretching into the haze. She had always sailed toward the *future* like a headwind — leaning in, never back — but tonight the islands ahead seemed to lean away from her.
future:1.cnHint: 银牙站在灯塔高处，望向迷雾中那片象征____的群岛。
future:1.hook: One island had not been there yesterday.
future:1.line: 'The *future* is another island — you sail to it or you don't,' Silverfang said.

effect:1.en: Bell lit the small lantern she carried and held it up to the lighthouse lens. The *effect* was immediate: a ring of coloured light spread across the stone courtyard, and shapes that had been invisible on the floor blazed into a clear pattern.
effect:1.cnHint: 贝尔用小灯笼照向灯塔镜片，光的____令隐藏的图案浮现。
effect:1.hook: The pattern pointed toward a door no one had noticed.
effect:1.line: 'I did not expect that *effect*,' Bell whispered, stepping back.

local:1.en: A group of *local* islanders gathered near the lighthouse gate as we arrived. They spoke quietly among themselves and kept their eyes on Old Helm. One of them held a small flag — the colour of which matched the mark on the fragment we had been carrying.
local:1.cnHint: 一群____岛民聚集在灯塔门口，其中一人手持的旗帜暗藏玄机。
local:1.hook: None of them looked surprised to see us.
local:1.line: 'The *local* people here know something we don't,' Old Helm said.

tend:1.en: Old Helm noticed that the lighthouse flame never flickered, even when the wind was strong. 'Flames *tend* to follow the wind,' he said, frowning. Bell agreed — every fire she had ever watched bent and danced, yet this one stood perfectly still, as if held by an unseen hand.
tend:1.cnHint: 老舵发现灯塔的火焰异常稳定，火焰____顺风而动，但这团火纹丝不动。
tend:1.hook: Bell reached out and felt no heat at all.
tend:1.line: 'Flames *tend* to move, but this one has forgotten how,' Old Helm said.

term:1.en: The inscription above the lighthouse door used a *term* none of us recognised — two carved words in an old island tongue. Bell copied it carefully into her log. Old Helm stared at it for a long moment, then said he had heard it once before, in a story he thought was only a story.
term:1.cnHint: 灯塔门楣上有一个古老的____，老舵曾在一个传说中听过它。
term:1.hook: He would not say where — or when.
term:1.line: 'That *term* is the lighthouse's true name,' Old Helm said quietly.

reduce:1.en: At the edge of Driftstone Dock, Old Helm studied the old lighthouse. Its great beam had once swept the whole sky, but something was wrong. Each night the light grew weaker. 'We must *reduce* the fog lanterns around it,' he said, 'so the beam can breathe again.'
reduce:1.cnHint: 老舵手认为，只有____周围多余的雾灯，灯塔的主光才能恢复往日的亮度。
reduce:1.hook: But the fog lanterns were already cold and dark.
reduce:1.line: 'We must *reduce* the fog lanterns, or the beam will die tonight.'

process:1.en: Bell spread the map across the dock boards and traced each step with her finger. Finding a lost lighthouse word was never simple. 'The *process* takes patience,' she told me. 'First we read the wind, then the stars, then the stone.' I watched and tried to remember every move.
process:1.cnHint: 领航员向我解释寻找灯塔词语的____，从风到星再到石头，一步都不能少。
process:1.hook: The third step — the stone — began to glow on its own.
process:1.line: 'The *process* takes patience, but the last step always surprises you.'

able:1.en: The lighthouse door was sealed with three iron locks. Old Helm tried each key on his ring, one by one, while the wind pushed hard against our backs. At last the third key turned, and we were *able* to step inside. The air smelled of old salt and something electric.
able:1.cnHint: 老舵手尝试了所有钥匙，终于____推开了那扇被三把锁封住的灯塔大门。
able:1.hook: Inside, the staircase spiralled down, not up.
able:1.line: 'At last we are *able* to enter — though I am not sure we should.'

drive:1.en: A cold wind rolled across Driftstone Dock without warning. It did not bend the lanterns or scatter the map. Instead, it seemed to *drive* us forward, pushing at our shoulders like a firm, patient hand. Bell laughed softly. 'The island wants us to hurry,' she said.
drive:1.cnHint: 一阵突如其来的冷风似乎在____我们加快脚步，仿佛这座岛屿也在催促大家。
drive:1.hook: The wind stopped the moment we reached the lighthouse door.
drive:1.line: 'Something is trying to *drive* us to that door — feel it?'

face:1.en: Halfway up the outer wall, carved into pale stone, was a giant *face*. Its eyes were closed, its mouth open just wide enough to hold a folded piece of paper. Old Helm reached in carefully and drew out a small, dry map fragment. 'The lighthouse was waiting,' he whispered.
face:1.cnHint: 灯塔外墙上刻着一张石头____，嘴里藏着我们一直在寻找的地图碎片。
face:1.hook: As Old Helm stepped back, the stone eyes slowly opened.
face:1.line: 'Look at that *face* — it has been holding our answer all along.'

possible:1.en: From the dock, I looked up at the dark lighthouse and felt doubt creep in. The word fragment could be anywhere inside — or it might not be there at all. Bell rested a hand on my shoulder. 'It is still *possible* we find it before dawn,' she said gently. I chose to believe her.
possible:1.cnHint: 领航员鼓励我，在天亮之前找到词语碎片依然是____的，不要放弃希望。
possible:1.hook: Dawn was only one hour away.
possible:1.line: 'It is still *possible* — I have seen stranger things found in darker places.'

similar:1.en: Old Helm held two map fragments side by side under the dock lantern. Their edges matched almost perfectly, and the star patterns on each looked *similar* enough to be twins. 'They come from the same island,' he decided. Bell nodded. I felt a quiet thrill run from my fingertips to my heels.
similar:1.cnHint: 老舵手发现两张地图碎片上的星图图案____得惊人，很可能来自同一座岛屿。
similar:1.hook: But one fragment carried a warning the other did not.
similar:1.line: 'These two patterns are *similar* — far too similar to be a coincidence.'

involve:1.en: Silverfang appeared at the far end of the dock, arms folded, watching us with narrow eyes. Old Helm sighed and turned to me. 'Every lighthouse mystery seems to *involve* him sooner or later,' he murmured. Bell was already checking the ropes on our sky-boat. Whatever came next, we would not wait around.
involve:1.cnHint: 老舵手叹气说，每一次灯塔谜题似乎总会____竞争船长的出现，让事情变得复杂。
involve:1.hook: Silverfang smiled and began walking slowly toward us.
involve:1.line: 'Why does every mystery have to *involve* you, Silverfang — every single time?'

put:1.en: The old lighthouse stood at the edge of the island, its lamp dark for years. Old Helm *put* a small glowing stone into the lamp's hollow centre, and the whole tower hummed to life, painting the night sky gold. A path of light stretched out across the clouds below us.
put:1.cnHint: 老赫姆把一块发光的石头____进灯塔的灯座，整座塔亮了起来。
put:1.hook: But the light was pointing somewhere it should not.
put:1.line: 'I *put* the stone in — now let's see where it leads.'

difference:1.en: Bell studied two old maps spread across the lighthouse steps. At first they looked the same, but she traced a thin line with her finger and smiled. 'The *difference* is right here,' she said. One map showed a hidden island that the other had left out completely. We all leaned in closer.
difference:1.cnHint: 贝尔发现两张地图之间有____，其中一张标出了一座隐藏的岛屿。
difference:1.hook: The hidden island had no name — only a single question mark.
difference:1.line: 'The *difference* between these maps tells us exactly where to go.'

lack:1.en: We climbed the lighthouse stairs to get a better view, but the thick cloud below made seeing almost impossible. Old Helm said our biggest problem was a *lack* of wind — without it, our ship could not reach the next island before the stars faded and the path disappeared. Time was short.
lack:1.cnHint: 老赫姆说，他们面临风力的____，无法在星光消失前赶到下一座岛。
lack:1.hook: Then, from somewhere deep in the clouds, a strange wind began to rise.
lack:1.line: 'A *lack* of wind is our only enemy right now.'

case:1.en: Bell pulled a small wooden *case* from her coat and opened it carefully. Inside lay a compass unlike any I had seen — its needle pointed not north but towards the brightest star overhead. 'Every navigator in our troupe has carried one of these,' she said, and handed it to me with a grin.
case:1.cnHint: 贝尔打开一个木制的____，里面装着一枚指向星星的特别罗盘。
case:1.hook: The needle suddenly spun three full turns and stopped dead.
case:1.line: 'This *case* holds the most important tool we own.'

sure:1.en: Standing on the lighthouse balcony, I looked out at three cloud roads leading in different directions. Old Helm crossed his arms and studied each one. 'I am *sure* the middle road is the right one,' he said quietly, 'because the stars above it are arranged like the old signal we learned long ago.'
sure:1.cnHint: 老赫姆____中间那条云路是正确的，因为它上方的星星排列像一个古老的信号。
sure:1.hook: A low rumble rose from the middle road before we even moved.
sure:1.line: 'I am *sure* — the middle road is where we need to go.'

enough:1.en: The lighthouse lamp burned bright, but Old Helm shook his head. 'It is not *enough*,' he said. 'The next island is too far — one stone alone cannot carry the light all the way.' Bell reached into her bag and produced two more glowing stones. Together, the three made the beam blaze like a second sun.
enough:1.cnHint: 一块发光石头的亮度不____，贝尔又拿出两块，三块合在一起光芒大盛。
enough:1.hook: In that blaze of light, a shape appeared on the distant clouds.
enough:1.line: 'One stone is never *enough* for a journey this long.'

attention:1.en: A sharp whistle cut through the night air. It was Silverfang, standing at the base of the lighthouse with her arms raised. 'Pay *attention* to the pattern on the door,' she called up to us. We had walked past it twice without noticing — carved into the stone was a map we had been searching for all day.
attention:1.cnHint: 西尔弗方提醒大家把____放在灯塔门上的图案——那正是他们寻找了一整天的地图。
attention:1.hook: Carved beside the map was a warning none of us could read.
attention:1.line: 'Pay *attention* — the answer has been on this door all along.'

certain:1.en: Silverfang met us on the open ledge outside the lighthouse, her silver coat bright under the stars. She pointed to a *certain* cluster of lights far below the clouds. 'That group of lamps never moves,' she said. 'It marks a fixed island — a real one, not a drifting ghost.' Old Helm immediately unrolled his chart.
certain:1.cnHint: 西尔弗方指出云层下____一组灯光从不移动，那标志着一座真实的固定岛屿。
certain:1.hook: Old Helm's finger landed on a spot the chart had left blank.
certain:1.line: 'There is a *certain* cluster of lights that never drifts — follow it.'

survey:1.en: Old Helm led us to the edge of the highest island and asked me to *survey* the broken bridges below. I counted seven gaps, each one wider than the last. He needed to know which path our troupe could cross before the star-tide turned.
survey:1.cnHint: 老舵手让我____周围断裂的桥梁，统计可能的通行路线。
survey:1.hook: The seventh gap breathed fog — something moved inside it.
survey:1.line: '*Survey* every gap carefully before you mark the map,' Old Helm said.

care:1.en: Bell wrapped the newly found word-fragment in soft cloth with great *care*, as if it were made of light itself. The fragment pulsed faintly, warming her hands. Around us the island hummed, and even the wind seemed to slow down to watch.
care:1.cnHint: 领航员以极大的____保护刚刚发现的词语碎片。
care:1.hook: The fragment pulsed once — and the island tilted slightly east.
care:1.line: 'Handle it with *care*,' Bell said, 'or the map will rewrite itself.'

state:1.en: The old lighthouse stood in a sorry *state*: its lamp was dark, its steps were cracked, and moss covered every stone. Old Helm walked a slow circle around it, saying nothing. I felt sure the lighthouse had once guided whole fleets of sky-ships home.
state:1.cnHint: 古老的灯塔处于破败的____，老舵手沉默地绕着它踱步。
state:1.hook: Then one cracked step shifted — and a hidden door opened.
state:1.line: 'Look at the *state* of this place,' Old Helm said quietly.

impact:1.en: The word-fragment hit the lighthouse stone with a sharp *impact*, and a ring of blue light spread outward across the whole island floor. We stepped back. Slowly, a new path of floating stones rose from the clouds below, pointing toward a distant island none of us had seen before.
impact:1.cnHint: 词语碎片撞击石壁的____让整座岛屿亮起蓝光，新路随之浮现。
impact:1.hook: The new path ended at an island shaped like an open eye.
impact:1.line: 'Feel that *impact*?' Bell whispered. 'The whole island heard it.'

reason:1.en: I asked Old Helm why the lighthouse had gone dark. He smiled and said there was always a *reason* — we just had to find it. Bell pointed to a hollow in the wall where the word-stone should have sat. Someone had taken it long before we arrived.
reason:1.cnHint: 老舵手说灯塔熄灭一定有____，而领航员发现关键位置空空如也。
reason:1.hook: The hollow was still warm, as if the stone had just left.
reason:1.line: 'There is a *reason* for every darkness,' Old Helm said gently.

close:1.en: Silverfang's ship appeared from the clouds, flying *close* enough that I could see the silver flag snapping in the wind. Old Helm did not flinch. Bell checked her compass twice. We all knew that wherever the word-stone led, Silverfang would not be far behind.
close:1.cnHint: 竞争船长的飞船靠得很____，让众人意识到对手始终紧随其后。
close:1.hook: Silverfang raised one hand — not a threat, but a strange greeting.
close:1.line: 'They are too *close*,' Bell said. 'We move now.'

individual:1.en: Each word-fragment carried its own *individual* glow — some gold, some pale blue, and one a deep, steady green. No two felt the same in your hand. Bell kept them in separate pockets, saying that mixing them too early would confuse the map and send us somewhere none of us wanted to go.
individual:1.cnHint: 每一块词语碎片都有____的光芒，领航员分开存放以免地图出错。
individual:1.hook: The green fragment flickered — and pointed firmly toward the dark.
individual:1.line: 'Each one is *individual*,' Bell said, 'so keep them apart for now.'

area:1.en: We gathered outside the lighthouse and divided the surrounding *area* into four sections to search for the missing word-stone. Old Helm took the cliffs, Bell the tide-pools, and I took the star-moss fields. The wind carried a soft ringing sound from somewhere just beyond the edge.
area:1.cnHint: 众人将灯塔周围的____划分成四块，分头寻找失踪的词语石。
area:1.hook: The ringing grew louder — and it came from underground.
area:1.line: 'Search your *area* completely before you call out,' said Old Helm.

enable:1.en: At the edge of Windperch Island, Old Helm unrolled a glowing map fragment on a flat stone. 'This word will *enable* us to cross the cloud bridge,' he said, tracing the faint letters with one finger. The whole troupe leaned in, breath held, watching the bridge slowly rise from the mist below.
enable:1.cnHint: 老舵在悬崖边展开地图碎片，发现一个词能____我们穿越云桥。
enable:1.hook: But the bridge had only enough room for one.
enable:1.line: 'This word will *enable* us to cross — so who goes first?'

simple:1.en: Bell knelt beside a cracked signpost at the island's crossroads, studying the carved letters. The answer to the puzzle, she realised, was *simple* — three small words pointing the way north. She laughed softly, surprised that something so easy had kept the troupe guessing for an entire morning.
simple:1.cnHint: 领航员在路口研究路标，发现谜题的答案其实____得出人意料。
simple:1.hook: Then she noticed the fourth word, half-hidden by moss.
simple:1.line: 'The answer is *simple* — we just forgot to look down.'

several:1.en: Old Helm led us through a winding street of lantern-sellers on Amber Shelf Island. We had passed *several* dark doorways before Bell spotted a faint glow behind one of them, too steady to be a candle, too quiet to be a fire. She raised her hand and the troupe stopped.
several:1.cnHint: 我们在琥珀架岛的街道上经过了____扇黑暗的门，领航员发现其中一扇透出异样的光。
several:1.hook: Whatever waited inside was already watching us.
several:1.line: 'We have passed *several* strange doors — that one is different.'

struggle:1.en: The old rope ladder down to Lantern Dock swayed in the wind, and I could see every rung was slick with dew. My *struggle* to hold on was real — hands burning, boots slipping — but Old Helm's calm voice from below kept me moving one step at a time until solid ground met my feet.
struggle:1.cnHint: 通往灯笼码头的绳梯又滑又摇，"我"____着一步步向下爬，老舵在下方出声鼓励。
struggle:1.hook: Then the ladder snapped free from its top hook.
struggle:1.line: 'Your *struggle* is not weakness — it is how you learn the ropes.'

decision:1.en: At the fork in the floating road, Bell turned to Old Helm with a steady look. The left path led toward the lighthouse signal; the right, toward Silverfang's anchored ship. Every second spent thinking cost us light. Old Helm exhaled slowly — it was his *decision* to make, and we all knew it.
decision:1.cnHint: 在浮路的岔口，老舵要做一个____：去灯塔还是去银牙的船。
decision:1.hook: He pointed left — and Silverfang's lantern flared in the dark.
decision:1.line: 'The *decision* is mine, and I choose the lighthouse.'

kid:1.en: Near the base of the lighthouse, a small *kid* — a young goat — stood chewing the corner of a paper scroll. Bell gasped and gently pulled the scroll free. The letters on it matched the fragment Old Helm carried, meaning the goat had wandered here from exactly the place we needed to find.
kid:1.cnHint: 灯塔脚下，一只小____正在啃咬一张纸卷，领航员轻轻抽出后发现它正是我们寻找的线索。
kid:1.hook: The goat blinked once, then trotted into the fog.
kid:1.line: 'Follow that *kid* — it knows the way better than we do.'

ability:1.en: Silverfang leaned against a salt-worn post near the harbour entrance, arms crossed. 'I have watched your troupe all morning,' she said to Old Helm. 'Your navigator's *ability* to read island winds is rare.' It did not sound like a compliment. It sounded like the opening move of a very careful plan.
ability:1.cnHint: 银牙在港口入口处盯着我们看了一早晨，她对老舵说领航员有一种罕见的____。
ability:1.hook: Rare enough, it seemed, that she wanted it for herself.
ability:1.line: 'Her *ability* to read the wind is something I have never seen.'

task:1.en: Old Helm handed me a small lantern and pointed toward the iron door at the lighthouse base. 'Your *task* is simple,' he said with a slight smile. 'Knock three times and ask for the keeper.' Simple, perhaps — but my hand trembled as the lantern light caught the carvings around the door's edge.
task:1.cnHint: 老舵交给"我"一盏灯笼，说我的____很简单，只需敲门找守灯人，但门上的刻纹让我手心发抖。
task:1.hook: From behind the iron door came the sound of something sliding.
task:1.line: 'Your *task* is to knock and ask — nothing more, nothing less.'

popular:1.en: The market square on Lantern Isle buzzed with colour. Every stall sold a different kind of star-fruit, and the crowd pressed close to the brightest one. 'This vendor is the most *popular* on the whole island,' Bell said, lifting onto her toes to see. Old Helm handed me a coin and smiled. 'Go find out why.'
popular:1.cnHint: 在灯笼岛的集市上，小铃指着人群最密集的摊位，说它是全岛最____的。
popular:1.hook: But the vendor's cart held something far stranger than fruit.
popular:1.line: 'This stall is the most *popular* on the island — and I think I know the secret.'

current:1.en: We stood at the edge of Lantern Isle, watching the wind carry glowing seeds across the sky. Bell held up a small flag to read the direction. 'The *current* air stream runs east tonight,' she said quietly. Old Helm nodded and unrolled the next map piece. The seeds were drifting straight toward a place none of us had named yet.
current:1.cnHint: 小铃举起小旗，判断今晚____的气流方向，老舵手展开了下一片地图。
current:1.hook: The unnamed island blinked once, like a sleeping eye opening.
current:1.line: 'The *current* wind is east — we should leave before it shifts.'

difficult:1.en: The old lighthouse door was sealed with a word-lock, its letters worn smooth by years of salt wind. I tried every combination I could think of. Old Helm crossed his arms and watched. 'It is *difficult*, but not impossible,' he said. 'Think about what a lighthouse does, not what it looks like.' The answer arrived in my mind like a struck match.
difficult:1.cnHint: 灯塔的门设有文字密锁，老舵手提示我，解开它____但并非不可能。
difficult:1.hook: The door creaked open onto a staircase full of soft, humming light.
difficult:1.line: 'It is *difficult*, yes — but the right word always fits in the end.'

amount:1.en: Inside the lighthouse store-room, jars lined every shelf from floor to ceiling. Each jar held a single glowing word, sealed tight. Bell counted under her breath and turned to me wide-eyed. 'The *amount* of words here could map a hundred new islands,' she whispered. Old Helm placed one careful hand on my shoulder. 'And every one was found by someone just like you.'
amount:1.cnHint: 灯塔储藏室里摆满了装着发光文字的罐子，小铃惊叹这里文字的____足以绘制百座新岛的地图。
amount:1.hook: One jar near the back pulsed with a light none of us recognised.
amount:1.line: 'The *amount* of words in here is beyond anything I expected.'

point:1.en: Old Helm spread the collected map pieces on the lighthouse floor. He tapped the very centre where all the lines met. 'This is the *point* we have been moving toward all along,' he said, his voice low and warm. Bell and I leaned in. The shape that formed was not an island. It was a door, drawn in starlight, standing in open sky.
point:1.cnHint: 老舵手将所有地图碎片拼在一起，指着交汇处说，那才是他们一直前进的____所在。
point:1.hook: The door in the map began to glow gold at its edges.
point:1.line: 'Look here — this is the *point* where every path we have walked meets.'

role:1.en: Silverfang arrived just as we were about to leave, her ship sliding alongside the lighthouse rock. She looked at the map, then at me. 'Every troupe needs a word-finder,' she said, almost gently. 'That is your *role* now.' Old Helm said nothing, but the small nod he gave me meant more than any speech. I folded the map and tucked it close.
role:1.cnHint: 银牙船长看着地图，告诉我"寻词者"是我在队伍中的____，老舵手点头默认。
role:1.hook: Beyond the lighthouse, a new island rose slowly from the clouds.
role:1.line: 'A word-finder is a vital *role* — do not carry it lightly.'

risk:1.en: The old lighthouse leaned over the edge of the floating island, half its base crumbling into open sky. 'We need that beacon to read our map fragment,' said Old Helm. I looked down at the endless drop below. To reach the lamp room, I would have to *risk* a climb along the cracked outer wall.
risk:1.cnHint: 灯塔摇摇欲坠，我必须攀上破裂的外墙才能拿到地图碎片，这太危险了——老舵长说我们必须____这一切。
risk:1.hook: One loose stone, and the stars would swallow me whole.
risk:1.line: 'We must *risk* the climb — there is no other way up,' said Old Helm.

success:1.en: Bell had mapped the approach three times before dawn. She marked every cracked tile, every gust of wind that swept the lighthouse platform. When I finally set the beacon turning and light poured across the dark clouds below, she raised both arms. 'That,' she said quietly, 'is a *success* worth remembering.'
success:1.cnHint: 贝尔在黎明前反复规划路线，当灯塔终于亮起，她说这次____值得铭记。
success:1.hook: But the light was spelling something — a message no one expected.
success:1.line: 'A *success* like this means the next island will show itself,' said Bell.

group:1.en: Three other travellers were already camped at the base of the lighthouse when we arrived — a cartographer, a wind-reader, and a lantern-keeper. Old Helm studied them with quiet eyes. 'Every strong *group* needs different kinds of knowing,' he said, and walked over to introduce us all before the stars shifted overhead.
group:1.cnHint: 灯塔脚下聚集着一小**** 旅行者，老舵长说每个优秀的____都需要不同的才能。
group:1.hook: The lantern-keeper smiled and said she had been waiting for us.
group:1.line: 'A *group* this varied can solve puzzles none of us could alone,' said Old Helm.

course:1.en: The map fragment from the lighthouse showed a winding path through three cloud-banks before reaching the next island. Bell traced it with one finger. 'The *course* is longer than I hoped,' she admitted, 'but it curves past the Wind Garden — and that means we can resupply before the cold stretch ahead.'
course:1.cnHint: 灯塔碎片揭示了一条曲折的____，贝尔说虽然路途更远，但能经过风之花园补给。
course:1.hook: Something was already moving along that course — and moving fast.
course:1.line: 'The *course* bends wide, but trust me — it is the safer road,' said Bell.

relationship:1.en: Silverfang's ship had been circling the lighthouse island since morning. He and Old Helm stood a short distance apart on the stone platform, speaking in low, careful voices. I had always wondered about their history. 'Our *relationship* is complicated,' Old Helm told me later, eyes on the horizon, 'but never dishonest.'
relationship:1.cnHint: 银牙在灯塔岛附近徘徊，老舵长说他们之间的____复杂，但从不欺骗对方。
relationship:1.hook: Silverfang glanced back once, and his expression was hard to read.
relationship:1.line: 'Our *relationship* goes back further than this troupe does,' said Old Helm.

form:1.en: The lighthouse door was sealed with a strange lock — a flat stone panel covered in carved symbols. Bell ran her hand across it slowly. 'Each symbol is a letter,' she said, 'and together they *form* a word that must be spoken aloud.' The wind held still, as if the island itself was listening.
form:1.cnHint: 灯塔大门被符文封印，贝尔说这些符号拼在一起会____一个必须大声说出的词。
form:1.hook: She whispered the word, and the stone door began to breathe.
form:1.line: 'These carvings *form* the oldest word in any map we have carried,' said Bell.

interest:1.en: Old Helm did not often stop walking, but the carved mural along the lighthouse wall made him pause. He leaned close, reading lines of ancient script that described the first travellers to cross these skies. 'I have a deep *interest* in whoever built this place,' he murmured, almost to himself, as the stars above brightened.
interest:1.cnHint: 灯塔外墙的壁画让老舵长驻足，他说自己对建造这座灯塔的人有着深厚的____。
interest:1.hook: One face in the mural looked unsettlingly familiar.
interest:1.line: 'My *interest* in this lighthouse began long before we arrived here,' said Old Helm.

simply:1.en: The beacon at the top of the lighthouse had not turned in years; its gears were clogged with salt and dust. I expected a long repair, but Bell opened a small panel, pressed two brass buttons, and the whole mechanism hummed to life. Some things, I realised, are *simply* waiting for someone willing to try.
simply:1.cnHint: 灯塔的旋转灯机年久失修，贝尔轻轻按下按钮，一切____就恢复了运转。
simply:1.hook: The light swept out — and landed on a shape in the clouds.
simply:1.line: 'It was *simply* waiting for steady hands and a little courage,' said Bell.

conversation:2.en: Inside the lighthouse, we found two stone chairs facing each other, a cold cup of tea between them. Old Helm knelt and studied the dust. 'Someone sat here not long ago,' he said. The *conversation* between those two visitors had left its mark — notes scratched into the armrests, word after word.
conversation:2.cnHint: 灯塔内两把石椅之间，老舵手发现了一段____留下的痕迹。
conversation:2.hook: One scratched word matched our next map fragment exactly.
conversation:2.line: 'That *conversation* was never finished,' Old Helm said softly.

self:2.en: Bell found a small mirror nailed to the lighthouse wall at eye level. Below it, someone had carved a single line into the stone. Old Helm read it aloud: 'To know the path, first know your *self*.' Bell stared at her own reflection for a long moment, then quietly nodded.
self:2.cnHint: 灯塔墙上的镜子旁刻着一句话，领航员盯着____的倒影若有所思。
self:2.hook: Her reflection seemed to mouth a word none of us could read.
self:2.line: 'Your *self* is the compass that never breaks,' Bell whispered.

age:2.en: The lighthouse keeper's log sat on a high shelf, its cover soft with dust. Old Helm opened it with careful hands. The first page held only a date — centuries past — and a single note: 'This *age* of floating islands began with one lost word.' We looked at each other in silence.
age:2.cnHint: 灯塔日志的扉页记录了浮岛____的起源，让众人陷入沉默。
age:2.hook: The date in the log was older than our oldest map.
age:2.line: 'Every *age* leaves one secret it cannot keep,' Old Helm murmured.

future:2.en: Tucked beneath the lighthouse lens, we found a sealed envelope addressed to no one. Inside was a short letter that began: 'To whoever finds this — the *future* of these islands depends on the words still lost.' Bell's hands trembled as she read. The letter was signed with only a star.
future:2.cnHint: 镜头下藏着一封信，信中说浮岛的____取决于那些尚未找到的词语。
future:2.hook: The ink was still faintly warm, as if written moments ago.
future:2.line: 'The *future* is already listening,' Bell read aloud, her voice unsteady.

effect:2.en: Old Helm lit the lighthouse lamp as a test. The beam swept across the fog outside, and something unexpected happened — distant islands we had never seen before appeared, glowing faintly. 'The *effect* of this light is more than guidance,' he said, eyes wide. Bell was already drawing them onto the map.
effect:2.cnHint: 老舵手点亮灯塔时，灯光的____令迷雾中浮现出从未见过的岛屿。
effect:2.hook: Seven new islands shimmered, then one slowly began to rise.
effect:2.line: 'The *effect* fades by dawn — draw fast,' Old Helm urged.

local:2.en: A woman appeared at the lighthouse door, basket in hand, clearly surprised to find us inside. She was *local* to the nearest island cluster, she explained, and had tended this lighthouse since she was young. She set her basket down and offered us warm bread without being asked.
local:2.cnHint: 一位____居民出现在门口，她已照看这座灯塔多年。
local:2.hook: She knew Old Helm's name before he introduced himself.
local:2.line: 'We *local* keepers never let the light go out,' she said proudly.

tend:2.en: The lighthouse keeper's notes described a garden of glowing moss on the eastern face of the tower. Bell found it exactly where the notes said. 'Living things *tend* to grow toward light,' she said, touching the soft green glow gently. Beneath the moss, a carved word pulsed with faint warmth.
tend:2.cnHint: 领航员在灯塔东侧发现了苔藓花园，苔藓____朝着光生长，遮住了刻在下方的词语。
tend:2.hook: The word carved beneath glowed brighter as Bell's fingers drew near.
tend:2.line: 'Plants *tend* toward light — so do lost words,' Bell said.

term:2.en: The sealed drawer at the base of the lighthouse held a short contract between two captains. One *term* stood out, written larger than the rest: 'Whoever holds the final word holds the sky.' Old Helm read it twice, folded it carefully, and slipped it into his coat without explanation.
term:2.cnHint: 灯塔底部的密封抽屉里有一份合约，其中一项____让老舵手神色凝重。
term:2.hook: Old Helm's silence told us that term was already in play.
term:2.line: 'That *term* was never cancelled,' Old Helm said, folding the page.

reduce:2.en: Inside the lighthouse base, Bell found a brass dial covered in dust. She turned it slowly, and we watched the roaring wind outside begin to *reduce* to a gentle whisper. The tower hummed, as if it had been waiting years for someone to know the right touch.
reduce:2.cnHint: 小铃转动铜盘，将外面的风____到微弱的低语。
reduce:2.hook: But the silence that followed felt far too deliberate.
reduce:2.line: 'Turn it further — we can *reduce* the storm to nothing,' Bell said.

process:2.en: Old Helm spread the lighthouse log across the floor. Each page showed a careful *process*: light on, mirror angled, signal sent. Someone had used this tower not to guide ships, but to send a coded message — step by step — to somewhere far above the clouds.
process:2.cnHint: 老舵手发现灯塔日志记录着某个神秘的____。
process:2.hook: The final step in the log was dated yesterday.
process:2.line: 'Follow the *process* exactly — one mistake and the signal vanishes,' Old Helm warned.

able:2.en: The top chamber was locked tight, but Bell noticed a narrow pipe running along the wall. She was small and quick. She was *able* to slip through a side hatch the others had missed entirely, and her voice drifted down to us a moment later: 'There is something up here.'
able:2.cnHint: 小铃____钻过一个隐藏舱口，发现了上层密室。
able:2.hook: Then her voice went very quiet.
able:2.line: 'I am *able* to reach it — just give me one more moment,' Bell called.

drive:2.en: A cold current of air flowed up through the lighthouse floor, and Old Helm said it was no accident. Something below was using the *drive* of the wind itself as a power source, spinning hidden gears that none of us had seen. The whole tower was a machine.
drive:2.cnHint: 老舵手意识到风的____正在为灯塔内部的齿轮提供动力。
drive:2.hook: And the gears were speeding up.
drive:2.line: 'The *drive* of the wind below — it powers everything in this tower,' Old Helm murmured.

face:2.en: Carved into the stone wall near the lamp was a round *face* — not human, not animal, but something in between. Its eyes were two small holes, and when Bell held her lantern close, light passed through and painted a map of stars across the opposite wall.
face:2.cnHint: 石墙上刻着一张____，透过它的眼孔能投射出星图。
face:2.hook: One constellation on the map was not in any sky we knew.
face:2.line: 'Look at the *face* on the wall — its eyes are pointing somewhere,' Bell said softly.

possible:2.en: Old Helm studied the signal log and shook his head slowly. 'It is *possible* that someone on a higher island has been reading our every move,' he said. Bell and I exchanged a glance. The lighthouse was not abandoned — it had simply changed hands without anyone noticing.
possible:2.cnHint: 老舵手认为____有人一直在更高的岛屿上监视我们。
possible:2.hook: Somewhere above, a light blinked twice.
possible:2.line: 'It is *possible* we have been watched since we arrived,' Old Helm said quietly.

similar:2.en: Bell pulled two glass lenses from the lamp housing. They were *similar* in shape but ground at different angles, and when stacked they bent light into a tight, bright beam aimed at a tiny notch in the far wall. Someone had designed this room as a lock, and light was the key.
similar:2.cnHint: 小铃发现两块____的镜片叠在一起，将光线引向墙上的缺口。
similar:2.hook: The notch opened with a soft, certain click.
similar:2.line: 'These two lenses are *similar* enough — stack them and see what happens,' Bell said.

involve:2.en: The coded message on the wall was longer than it first appeared. Old Helm read aloud, his voice growing careful: 'The path forward will *involve* the three voices of the lighthouse — wind, light, and bell.' He looked at Bell. She looked at the ceiling. We all heard the faint tone ringing above us.
involve:2.cnHint: 墙上的密文揭示，前进之路将____灯塔的三种声音。
involve:2.hook: The tone grew louder, as if it already knew her name.
involve:2.line: 'The next step will *involve* all three of us working at once,' Old Helm said.

suggest:2.en: The old lighthouse keeper had left no name, only a carved wooden board. Bell held it up to the starlight and traced each letter carefully. 'The marks *suggest* he sailed east,' she said, 'toward the island shaped like a sleeping bird.' Old Helm nodded slowly, already turning the wheel.
suggest:2.cnHint: 小铃仔细研究灯塔里的木板，从上面的痕迹____出航海者曾向东航行。
suggest:2.hook: But no island east of here appeared on any map we carried.
